A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GimbalDiffusion and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting comparison. Both end with references; neither includes the separately cited supplementary material, whose contents cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments on SpatialVID-extreme, quantitative baseline comparisons in Table 1, and a null-pitch ablation in Table 2.

after.justification: v2 reports revised SpatialVID-extreme experiments and ablations in Table 1, plus original prompt-camera entanglement experiments on PolyHaven panoramas in Section 4.6 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: The main model changes from CogVideoX-2B with an AC3D-style ControlNet to WAN-2.2 5B with a convolutional camera encoder and joint backbone finetuning. Section 3.2 adds gravity estimation from eight perspective views and changes pose composition. Section 3.3 adds downward-view captions and negative-prompt guidance to suppress tripods and other capture artifacts.

E1.justification: v2 adds PolyHaven panorama evaluation with viewpoint-specific reference content for prompt-camera disambiguation, alongside the retained SpatialVID-extreme video benchmark. The reported training source changes from WEB360 to a filtered PanoVid YouTube subset. Figure 2 also introduces a full-rotation, return-to-start test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds UCPE and PreciseCam+GEN3C while retaining both AC3D variants and PreciseCam+WAN. The SpatialVID qualitative comparison replaces PreciseCam+WAN with PreciseCam+GEN3C and adds UCPE. UCPE also joins the prompt-camera entanglement comparison in Figure 6.

E3.justification: The reported training setup changes from a 2B backbone trained for approximately 8,000 iterations to a 5B backbone jointly finetuned for 30,000 iterations. SpatialVID evaluation now specifies ViPE-derived metric translations instead of reusing original translations. The new entanglement protocol evaluates 20 panoramas at 19 static pitches and computes CLIP against pitch-specific reference captions.

E4.justification: The existing null-pitch ablation is retained under the revised setup and incorporated into Table 1. Section 4.6 adds a systematic pitch-sensitivity analysis testing prompt-camera conflicts across 380 conditions, extending v1's qualitative illustration. Figure 2 adds a full-rotation case study comparing trajectory adherence and return-view consistency.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars for the experimental results. The new aggregate curves in Figure 6 do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces numerical results for the proposed method and retained baselines, and adds comparator results. Reported pitch/gravity errors for Ours change from 23.79/27.06 to 9.35/11.67 under changed training and method conditions, not a controlled same-setting comparison. Unlike v1's ablation, v2 shows that null-pitch conditioning improves camera metrics but worsens CLIP, FID, and FVD relative to its ablated model. Figure 6 adds pitch-dependent findings.

T1.justification: Equation (2) substantively revises the absolute-pose construction by introducing gravity alignment through psi and separate translation and rotation expressions. This is a focused change to the mathematical definition of pose composition; neither version contains a theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The contribution list expands from one benchmark to two, making prompt-camera entanglement evaluation an explicit contribution. v1's conclusion claims the first absolute camera-control method for text-to-video; v2 drops that priority claim and positions the contribution around extreme and full-360-degree rotations. Gravity alignment and null-pitch conditioning remain central.

C2.justification: v1 attributes reduced CLIP and visual-quality scores primarily to training-data differences. v2 develops a substantive alternative interpretation: prompt-based CLIP can penalize correct camera views when requested content should be outside the frame. It also explains why null-pitch captions can induce capture artifacts and qualifies GEN3C comparisons because that method cannot generate scene motion.

D1.justification: v2 documents resolution and pose-quality filtering, retention of 4,798 of 7,797 training videos, 720-by-480 sampling, and variable prompt lengths. It adds camera-encoder initialization, AdamW settings, and a one-day training duration on eight H200 GPUs, replacing v1's four-A100 training description. Both still defer some implementation details to unavailable supplementary material.

R1.justification: Section 2 introduces UCPE as a concurrent gravity-aware alternative and substantially expands positioning against panoramic video generation and static novel-view synthesis. New discussions include GEN3C, ViewCrafter, PanoWAN, and PanFlow, with arguments about rotation diversity, cropped resolution, prompt visibility, and translation control. This changes the novelty argument beyond adding citations.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around extreme rotations and two evaluation goals. Related-work explanations are expanded and reorganized, gravity annotation precedes path sampling, and experimental exposition is reworked. The separate discussion and conclusion sections are merged into Section 5.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the teaser and reference-matching examples, redraws the pipeline, and replaces Euler-angle plots in the training examples with spatial camera trajectories. It redesigns the qualitative comparisons and expands Figure 6 into qualitative and quantitative panels. The ablation table is merged into a grouped Table 1; v1's distribution plot is absent from the supplied v2 pages.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important evidential gap by adding a controlled test of prompt-camera entanglement across pitches, beyond v1's general ablation and illustrative example. View-specific reference captions address a concrete metric mismatch, while UCPE provides a directly relevant gravity-aware comparator. Expanded implementation details also improve reproducibility. Changed backbones and data prevent controlled cross-version performance claims, and centered CLIP curves and visual-quality tradeoffs limit stronger conclusions, but the gains in mechanism testing and comparison relevance substantially improve the paper.
